html:
The Armero tragedy was the destruction of the town of Armero in Colombia on 13 November 1985, when the Nevado del Ruiz volcano erupted and sent mudflows down on it. More than 20,000 of the town's roughly 29,000 people died.

The eruption itself was small. But its heat melted part of the ice cap on the summit, and the meltwater mixed with ash and rock into fast moving mudflows called lahars. They rushed down the river valleys and reached Armero, about 70 km away, a couple of hours later, burying it in mud.

It need not have happened. The volcano had been restless for a year, and scientists had drawn a hazard map that showed Armero in danger. But officials did not order an evacuation.

The world remembers it through Omayra Sánchez, a 13 year old girl trapped in the ruins for three days, filmed and photographed before she died. It was the deadliest eruption since Mount Pelée in 1902, and it changed how scientists and governments plan for volcanic danger. It came only weeks after the Mexico City earthquake.
